info.title: NativeAuthOAuth API
info.description: Reusable passwordless user-authentication system. Native mode signs users in with one-time email links; a configuration switch (ENV_SIGNIN_METHOD=oauth) moves the deployment to OAuth social providers exclusively, disabling every native email flow. Sessions ride the single `session_token` cookie (httpOnly, secure, sameSite=lax).

tags.name: admin-polls
tags.description: Poll authoring/moderation. Administrators (ENV_ADMINS) act on every poll. A user holding both the Create Poll and View Polls grants may create polls, list only the polls they created, and act on those polls; any other poll answers 404. Search and rescreen stay administrator-only.

isAdmin.description: 012 FR-049/FR-052: whether this user may administer polls, computed by the same allow-list predicate that gates every admin route so the two can never drift. Every admin API and page route enforces the allow-list itself, so a user who forges this flag reveals a menu entry whose target still returns 403. A RENDERING HINT ONLY, like isAdmin — it decides whether the header's Create Poll link is live and whether a card offers a vote. Every route enforces the grants itself.

post.summary: Create a pending account and auto-send the first login link
post.description: The response is identical whether or not the address is already registered (account-existence privacy); an existing account receives a normal login link instead of a duplicate account. An address is matched to an existing account by its email key (plus-tag dropped; Gmail dots removed), so a variant of an existing address signs that account in. The request must carry the agreement to the current Terms of Service; the account records the version and the time. Token form: with `token` (the one-time link emailed to an address with no account), no `email` is sent; the server checks Origin, the token, the Terms (for an address still without an account), the rate limit and the allowlist, then creates the account, uses the token up and signs in at once, answering `{ redirect }` with the session cookie; no second email is sent.

get.summary: Consume a one-time login link
get.description: Self-contained — no session required. When the bind parameter matches the signin_binding cookie of the requesting browser, the link is consumed: success activates a pending account, revokes any other session (single active session per account), sets the session_token cookie (persistent iff staySignedIn was chosen), clears signin_binding and redirects to / (or to /?PID=<id> when the request carried a poll id). Otherwise a valid link is not consumed and redirects to /confirm-signin?token=…&stay=…[&PID=…]. Any failure (expired, used, superseded, malformed) redirects to /login?error=invalid-link (with &PID=<id> when one was carried) without revealing why.

pollState.description: 012 FR-024..FR-028. OPEN is allowed from WAITING TO OPEN or CLOSED; CLOSED from WAITING TO OPEN or OPEN; ARCHIVED only from CLOSED. Any other from-state is a 409 that leaves the poll unchanged. Each transition also writes the schedule so the date sweep confirms it rather than reverting it: OPEN clears startAt and clears endAt only if already past; CLOSED sets endAt to now and clears startAt only if in the future; ARCHIVED writes nothing but the state, preserving the poll's real closing date.

post.description: Replaces autosave: nothing reaches the server until this call, so a half-finished edit can never become public. Returns immediately — the screening outcome arrives later from pollsAwaitingApprovalSweep. In UPDATE mode only title, subtitle, startAt, endAt, the participant lists, the voter count limit and colors are accepted.

voterCountLimit.description: 012 FR-006..FR-009, FR-061, FR-064: null on a Public Poll (forced, whatever is sent); on a private poll an integer 1-500, where blank/null/empty-string all mean cleared and bind at 500. Accepted in UPDATE mode as well as EDIT: the limit is the poll's capacity rather than the meaning of a vote, so it stays editable once votes exist.

labels.description: 012 FR-011/FR-013: the poll's choice list, replacing the deleted PUT .../choices route. Accepted in EDIT mode only; in UPDATE mode it joins the disallowed fields and the whole save is refused with 400. Validated in the same pass as every other field and written in the same operation, so a rejected publish persists nothing.

invitedVoterList.description: 012 FR-059: the poll's invited list, as the desired final state. Replaces the deleted POST .../invited route — participant changes now save with the poll so Cancel can discard them. Accepted in both EDIT and UPDATE mode.

bannedVoterList.description: 012 FR-059: the poll's banned list, as the desired final state. Replaces the two deleted DELETE routes. Banning an address also removes it from the invited list and deletes its vote; un-banning restores neither (FR-017a).

colors.description: One bar color per entry of labels, in the same order: a palette hex code (any letter case, stored in the palette's spelling), a color the poll already stores on a choice, or null for Automatic. A list of a different length, or any other entry, is refused with 400 and nothing is saved. Labels sent without colors replace the choices with none colored. Sent alone, it sets the colors of the existing choices by position and changes no id, label or vote.

timeZone.description: The creator's IANA time zone (e.g. America/New_York), stored as the poll's time zone for the dates in its invitation emails. An invalid or missing zone is ignored, never refused; it changes no content version, state or review.

message.description: Present only when a poll that has not been published yet was held back for still holding its starter choices (FR-024/FR-025).

200.description: Either AWAITING APPROVAL, or INITIALIZED with a message when the poll has not been published yet and still holds its starter choices. A published poll is always sent for review.

400.description: Field outside the four permitted in UPDATE mode, over-length text, or startAt not before endAt

409.description: The poll is locked, awaiting approval, or archived

post.summary: Save a new poll without publishing it
post.description: Stores the answers of a poll that has not been published (INITIALIZED, or EDITING from INITIALIZED) and leaves it INITIALIZED, so the administrator can finish it later. Ends the editing session. Never requests approval. The body and the validation are those of /publish, except for an empty title and the number of choices. A poll that is not being edited is saved without a session, as /publish allows.

title.description: An empty title is ignored, so the stored title stays.

keywords.description: Search keywords, separated by commas: each lower-case letters, digits and single spaces, with no repeats; at most 200 characters in total. Always empty on a Private Poll (sent or not); frozen once the poll has ever been voted on.

pollVisibility.description: Whether the poll is open to everyone or restricted. One of three settings with pollSharingMode and voteAnonymity. Stored and displayed with identical wording — there is no code-to-label map. Frozen once the poll has ever been voted on.

pollSharingMode.description: For a private poll, whether anyone with the link may take part or only invited addresses. Always present; ignored while the poll is public. Frozen once the poll has ever been voted on.

voteAnonymity.description: For a private poll, whether the poll creator may see who voted for which choice (No) or totals only (Yes). Always present; ignored while the poll is public. Not yet read by anything: enforcement arrives with the poll creator role. Frozen once the poll has ever been voted on.

Accepted in UPDATE mode as well as EDIT: the limit is the poll's capacity rather than the meaning of a vote, so it stays editable once votes exist.

labels.description: The choices so far: 0 to ENV_MAX_CHOICES non-blank labels. With none, the stored choices stay; fewer than ENV_MIN_CHOICES are allowed, since nothing is published.

bannedVoterList.description: 012 FR-059: the poll's banned list, as the desired final state. Replaces the two deleted DELETE routes. Banning an address also removes it from the invited list and deletes its vote; un-banning restores neither (FR-017a).

colors.description: One bar color per entry of labels, in the same order: a palette hex code (any letter case, stored in the palette's spelling), a color the poll already stores on a choice, or null for Automatic. A list of a different length, or any other entry, is refused with 400 and nothing is saved. Labels sent without colors replace the choices with none colored. Ignored when no label is sent.

post.summary: Add, remove or remind invitees
post.description: Exactly one of add, remove and resend. Never changes the poll's state, edit session or review, and never pauses voting. On an OPEN poll added addresses are emailed after the response, within the creator's daily allowance (ENV_MAX_INVITATIONS_PER_DAY); otherwise they wait, Not sent yet, until the poll opens. An address removed after being emailed and added back keeps its earlier sent and reminded times and is not emailed again.

timeZone.description: The creator's IANA time zone (e.g. America/New_York), stored as the poll's time zone for the dates in its invitation emails. An invalid or missing zone is ignored, never refused; it changes no content version, state or review.

resend.description: The invitee to send the one reminder to; it is sent after the response.

timeZone.description: The creator's IANA time zone (e.g. America/New_York), stored as the poll's time zone for the dates in its invitation emails. An invalid or missing zone is ignored, never refused; it changes no content version, state or review.

waiting.description: added on an OPEN poll past the creator's daily allowance: it waits as Not sent yet and is sent as the rolling 24 hours free up.
